congregation

/kong-grih-GAY-shun/ · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Congregation means a group of people gathered together — especially the members of a church, synagogue, mosque, or temple who meet for worship.

The synagogue's congregation collected eight hundred cans of food for the community drive, and every Friday evening the same congregation fills the hall for prayers.

Example

Over three years, the mosque's congregation raised enough money to build the new prayer hall it had long dreamed of.

The congregation is the community of worshippers itself — the gathered members who pray, plan, and raise funds together as one body.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

assembly: An assembly is a formal gathering called together for a program or purpose — a school assembly, a legislative assembly — and it ends when the meeting ends. A congregation is a standing community of worshippers that exists between services, not just an audience summoned for one event.

flock: Flock is the affectionate, pastoral word for a religious community, picturing worshippers as a shepherd's charge — it is how a minister speaks of her own people. Congregation is the neutral, formal term for the same worshipping community, usable on a sign or in the news.

parish: A parish is the local district a church serves, and everyone who lives within its bounds — churchgoers or not. A congregation is the worshipping community itself: the members who actually gather for services, wherever they happen to live.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

dispersal: a breaking up and drifting apart

exodus: a mass departure

Where it sits · how much shared purpose unites the crowd

gathering → congregation → throng

gathering vs. congregation: A gathering is any casual group of people who happen to come together, with no special bond required — looser than a congregation, whose members are united by shared worship or purpose.

throng vs. congregation: A throng is far larger and denser than a typical congregation — a packed, pushing crowd that fills every inch of space.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — con-: together, with (Latin)

Root — greg: flock, herd (from Latin grex, gregis)

Suffix — -ation: the action or result of

Put it together: A congregation is literally the result (-ation) of flocking (grex) together (con-) — people drawn into one flock, which is why a religious community and its shepherd-like leader fit the word so naturally.

Use the root in a new word: gregarious: My gregarious uncle drifts from table to table at every family reunion, chatting happily with the whole flock.

Root Check

Word Choice

Religious / community

Today congregation almost always means the community of worshippers at a church, synagogue, mosque, or temple — both the people in the pews on a given day and the membership as a whole. In older or more formal writing it can name any assembled group; nineteenth-century authors even wrote of 'a congregation of birds' on a rooftop.
